如何看待今年湖北702分学霸遗憾错失清华北大，最终就读南大计算机？

强基锁档，高考超常发挥。鉴定完毕。

湖北省排22，够得着清北这块牌子，但够不够得着清北计算机。尤其姚班、图灵班那一档，完全是另一回事。
而南京大学的计算机和人工智能实力在国内处于绝对的第一梯队，其计算机软件新技术国家重点实验室以及周志华教授领衔的团队，在国际上都享有盛誉。

所以，可不可惜，全看信哪头。
信清北招牌和清华计算机的天花板值得赌那一把，那提前锁档确实把上限让出去了。信确定的顶配好过赌来的顶配的话，个人认为，这是笔风控做得挺不错的选择。

Finalmente lo tira (y falla) Tah, en lo que fue su 1º penalti como jugador profesional.

Y yo aquí nunca voy a culpar al que decide asumir la responsabilidad que otros no asumen, y por eso no voy a criticar a Tah por fallar el penalti decisivo.

La crítica va al tipo de 31 años que tiene un rol injustificado y que se hace pequeño en cada situación importante (desde hace 4 años, con club y selección).

PSA: We’ve reset Codex limits across plans and have added an additional banked reset!

Team spent the last 48 hours combing through each and every possibility and found a few issues:

> Auto-review and background suggestions were triggering too much unintended work, including duplicate runs and overly aggressive retries.

> We reverted the problematic changes and fixed scheduling, duplication, and retry behavior to reduce unnecessary background token usage.

> Usage reporting was also corrected: auto-review now has its own category, and failed or rate-limited requests no longer appear in turn graphs. Rate-limited requests were never charged.

Thanks a lot for your patience and for flagging issues as they roll! Enjoy the resets and keep codex-ing!!

Massive kudos to @ah20im and team for working over the weekend and seeing this through 🙏

quotedTweet.text:
Codex usage limits will be fully reset again in the next hour and we will credit one additional reset into your bank for your own usage over the next 24 hours.

We investigated reports that Codex usage was being consumed faster than expected. There wasn't one central issue, but a few smaller problems compounded for some users.   

Here's what we found and changed: 
- Actual usage: Auto-review had become more proactive, another change was triggering more subagent work, and background suggestions could run twice or retry too frequently after failures. We reverted the changes and fixed suggestion scheduling, duplicate generation, and retry behavior. This should reduce unnecessary background token consumption while preserving the work users explicitly request. 
- Usage reporting: Auto-review was incorrectly appearing as GPT‑5.4 usage, and failed or rate-limited requests were still shown as turns. Auto-review now appears as its own category, and only successful requests count toward the turn graphs. Rate-limited requests were never charged, but they were being displayed incorrectly. 
- Immediate relief: We reset usage limits while rolling out the fixes, then shipped hotfixes across the CLI, desktop app, and usage backend. 
- What to expect: New usage data should be clearer and actual consumption should be lower. Historical charts may still show auto-review under GPT‑5.4 because older turn data was not relabeled. Features that intentionally perform more work; such as /goal, subagents, and higher reasoning levels will still naturally use more capacity.  

All fixes are now deployed, and we've added more detailed monitoring so we can detect background-usage regressions sooner. We'll continue watching the results closely.

Thank you for building and doing all sorts of things with Codex.

text:
Someone ran Claude Code on an e-ink notebook and the slowest screen in the world suddenly turned out to be the best home for an AI that already thinks one word at a time.

This is the reMarkable Paper Pro, a paper tablet for notes with no browser and no social media and not a single app. He went into it over SSH and brought up Claude Code on Opus 4.8 on Claude Max and typed right into the terminal on the paper screen: "hello reddit, this is ssh terminal on rmpp".

For years this screen got slammed for one thing. E-ink is too slow and it draws with a delay and it ghosts and it is no good for real work. But Claude itself puts out a thought one word at a time.

And here is what came out of it: the very thing that killed the paper screen for normal software lined up perfectly with the pace of the AI. There is no more lag because there is nothing left to lag.

And then come the things no monitor can give you.

Your eyes do not get tired. You can watch Opus think on max effort for an hour and it feels like reading a book and not staring into a backlight.

Nothing distracts you. Not a single notification and not a single tab and just a cursor and an agent that writes code while you simply watch the page.

The charge lasts for days. E-ink barely touches the battery so Claude can grind on a task all night long and the tablet is still alive by morning.

And it weighs as much as a notebook. The whole work setup now fits into a bag like a notepad with a stylus on top.

Everything on the screen is for real: Claude Code v2.1.162 and bypass permissions on and Opus going off to think on max effort right on the e-ink.

In my opinion this is the most unexpected home for an AI this year.

Not a farm of graphics cards and not a wall of monitors but a quiet sheet of paper on a coffee table where the most powerful Claude writes code one word at a time like a pen.

"This is not a coincidence. On the side of the people in charge, this really does call for consequences. I can't put it any other way. Football is a results-oriented sport

text:
信任崩塌的那一瞬間，解釋是最沒用的武器。
​
昨天在一間建築師事務所做企業內訓，分享 NotebookLM 如何導入三個場景：會議記錄、法規糾錯、簡報製作。
​
一個半小時，三個 demo 全部跑完，節奏緊湊扎實。
​
中途，老闆提出一個問題：「我產出的內容跟他產出的內容對不起來。」
​
他臉上的表情，瞬間從期待轉成失望。
​
我當下的回答是：「可能是 PDF 檔案辨識不清，加上大語言模型本身也有隨機性導致。」
​
這句話是事實。
​
但他聽完，失望沒有消失，反而多了一層「這東西不可靠」的疑慮。
​
事後覆盤 After Action Review (AAR)，我才意識到那個回答答得不夠好。
​
我用的是「解釋」——解釋 PDF 的 OCR 辨識、大語言模型為什麼每個人會不一樣
​
這確實是事實，但信任崩塌的那一秒，事實從來不是最有效的武器。
​
如果可以重來，那個時候要做的是：立刻解決問題，不是解釋問題。
​
「老闆，讓我現在幫您重跑一遍——您能把文字版傳給我嗎？」
​
當場示範，當場拿到正確結果。
​
失望的表情，瞬間會變成「哇，他馬上解決了。」。
​
這個瞬間，才是贏得老闆信任、決定後續合作的關鍵轉折點

下次工作坊，提醒自己把「解釋問題」換成「解決問題（再解釋）」
​
AI 講師/顧問 之路，持續精進。

text:
Nagelsmanns Versagen beim DFB:
- Kein klares commitment zu Olli Baumann
- Kimmich ohne Not 3 mal im System verschoben, anstatt eine klare Rolle zu finden
- Pavlovics Position vor dem Turnier geändert, statt in die Kette zu fallen, Kimmich dorthin berufen und so beiden ihre Stärken genommen
- Keinen RV Backup (Treu) nominiert, damit nur ein System möglich gewesen
- Keine Struktur im Mittelfeld, innerhalb von 7 Spielen erst Goretzka, dann Stiller und dann Nmecha den Vorzug gegeben, nur damit am Ende keiner funktioniert
- festhalten an Leroy Sané, während Leweling genau diese Position in den besten Spielen ausgefüllt hat
- Wirtz und Musiala absolut falsch eingesetzt, Musiala nur einmal auf dem Flügel gespielt und dort auf der falschen Seite, Wirtz nie Zentral
- den Stammstürmer vor dem Turnier abrasiert, der dich überhaupt erst zur WM geführt hat
- fehlendes commitment zu einer klaren Strategie, klar gab es auch Verletzungen, aber das System mit dem man bei der WM erfolgreich war, wurde nur bis zum Wagner Abgang durchgezogen (das ja sogar sehr erfolgreich, unabhängig von Personalien)
- es verpasst junge Spieler mit Perspektive wie einen Urbig, Banks, Bischof, El Mala, Tresoldi etc in die Mannschaft zu implementieren, die letztendlich nicht einmal im Kader standen und für die Zukunft essentiell sind
- festhalten an Altstars über ihrem Zenit, die eine sehr schwache Form ins Turnier brachten
- es verpasst einen simplen Spielstil zu schaffen, der die Qualitäten der besten Spieler fördert
- nicht dazu in der Lage gewesen einen schnellen Ballbesitz mit viel Rotation in der Offensive zu spielen

Das größte Problem: All das hatte man, bevor es über den Haufen geworfen wurde und man sich dazu entschied biederen Fußball mit Altstars zu spielen

text:
منتخب النرويج دخل في ورطة... لكن ورطة جميلة. 😂🇳🇴

البعثة كانت عاملة حسابها على إن المشوار هيقف عند دور المجموعات، فخدت معاها كمية محددة من الأكل تكفي الفترة دي فقط.

سافروا بحوالي 300 كيلو من السلمون، والتروتة، والهلبوت، وأنواع الأسماك النرويجية، وكمان 180 كيلو من الجبن النرويجي.

لكن بعد التأهل إلى دور الـ32، لقوا نفسهم مضطرين يطلبوا شحنة جديدة من النرويج تكمل معاهم بقية البطولة. 😅

مش بس كده...

كانوا جايبين وافل ميكر، والمربى، والجبن البني، والقهوة النرويجية، عشان اللاعبين يحسوا إنهم في بيتهم.

أما هالاند، فاضطر يستغنى عن الحليب الخام المفضل عنده لأنه ممنوع في أمريكا، واستبدلوه بلبن منزوع اللاكتوز.

واضح إن النرويج كانت مستعدة لكل حاجة...

إلا إنها تكمل في كأس العالم لفترة أطول! 🇳🇴

text:
我特别喜欢和欣赏的一位连续创业者 @quxiaoyin 晓音，这两天在 X 上火起来了。

她提出一个很尖锐的判断：中国开源模型会持续获得市场份额，甚至可能成为美国 AI 生态的“最坏情境”之一—如果中国模型不仅占据 model layer，还逐步适配华为等国产芯片，叠加美国数据中心建设速度不够快，那么 AI 竞争就不只是模型之争，而是模型、芯片、算力、成本和生态的系统性竞争。

这个观点被 @a16z 创始人 Marc Andreessen  @pmarca  转发后，引起AI 圈大规模讨论。

我自己的看法是：open source / open-weight models 的重要性会越来越高。它们给企业带来更低成本、更强可控性、本地部署、私有数据微调，以及对单一闭源 API 供应商的议价能力。尤其当 AI 成本越来越高、地缘政治和合规限制越来越复杂时，开源模型会成为很多企业的战略选项。

但现在说谁会最终胜出，还太早。

闭源模型仍然在 frontier capability、稳定性、工具链、企业服务、安全合规、生态集成和品牌信任上有明显优势。未来更可能不是“开源打败闭源”或者“闭源统治一切”，而是一个混合格局：最前沿能力仍由少数闭源巨头推动，而大量应用层、企业层、本地化和成本敏感场景，会越来越依赖开放模型。

真正的竞争，可能不只是模型本身，而是谁能掌握完整生态：模型能力、推理成本、芯片适配、开发者社区、企业工作流、数据闭环和信任机制。

无论你是否完全同意晓音的判断，这都是一个值得认真讨论的问题：AI 的未来，到底会集中在少数闭源平台里，还是会被开放生态重新分散？

我做了一个 AI 中转站，今天正式开放：

https://t.co/8UjipCaDbh

一开始做这个站，想法很简单。

主要是我自己平时 Token 消耗量大，身边也有不少朋友一直用不上稳定的 Claude / GPT。不是订阅麻烦，就是各种限制；去找别的中转站，又总担心不靠谱、信息不安全。

所以干脆自己搭了一个。

很多人问：为什么敢用老叶的？

这个问题我也理解。毕竟 AI 中转站这东西，大家最怕的不是贵一点，而是不知道对面是谁。

我在币圈这么多年，别的不敢吹，信用两字一直是招牌。前两年比特币生态火的时候，做过 Ybot 铸造工具。起初也有人担心资产安全。

Ybot 到现在跑了两年多，上万人用过，很多人甚至直接在网站里填过钱包私钥，总资产少说也有几千万。到今天为止，没有出过一次因为网站原因导致的资产事故。

这次做 AI 中转站也是一样，稳定靠谱依然是我们的标签。

目前站里支持 GPT、Claude 等模型，底层用的是官方正规订阅账号池，不是乱七八糟的灰产号。价格这块也尽量压到较低，最低大概 0.7 折。

过去 10 天，我们做了一轮小范围内测：

✅ 200+ 小伙伴参与
✅ 累计消耗超过 420 亿 Token
✅ 整体运行稳定，没出明显故障

内测跑完之后，我觉得可以正式放出来给更多人用了。

需要稳定、便宜、靠谱的 Claude / GPT 中转站的，可以试试：

https://t.co/8UjipCaDbh

有问题可以直接私信我，或者进群找我。

老叶不跑路，真出问题我负责。

text:
In 2010, a massive earthquake struck Haiti killing over 220,000 Haitians and leaving more than 1.5 million homeless. Thousands of Haitians were permitted to enter the United States under Temporary Protected Status (TPS), a government program that allows refugees from countries experiencing environmental disaster, armed conflict or other life-threatening conditions to legally live and work temporarily in the United States.

Since the 2010 earthquake, 350,000 Haitian refugees have entered the United States under the TPS designation. The Trump administration, though, rightly points out that TPS is a temporary program. Since taking office, the Trump administration has attempted to deport the Haitians back to their home country, but were blocked by federal courts. The courts ruled that the Department of Homeland Security was unlawfully discriminating against Haitian immigrants on the basis of race.

On June 26, however, the Supreme Court reversed the lower court rulings and ruled that the Trump Administration can cancel the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) designation for Haiti (and Syria) forcing the refugees to return to their native countries.

But according to the United Nations and other reliable sources, the conditions in Haiti today are worse than they were in 2010. Wracked by hurricanes, earthquakes, and crime, Haiti is in a state of collapse. On October 29, 2025, Hurricane Melissa killed forty-three people and damaged or flooded nearly 12,000 houses. Armed gangs control an estimated 80 percent of Port-au-Prince, the national capital. Over 16,000 people have been killed since January 2022 and 1.5 million displaced from their homes. Half of the nation’s 11.9 million people face acute food shortages with 600,000 experiencing famine.

The U.S. State Department, warning Americans not to travel to Haiti, has assigned Haiti a Level 4 Travel Advisory, its highest warning, “due to the risk of crime, terrorism, kidnapping, unrest, and limited health care.” Commercial air travel to the country has been cancelled. For the few U.S. citizens still residing in Haiti, the State Department advises, “Consider hiring a professional security organization.”

Sending 350,000 Haitian refugees back to their native country will almost surely result in many of their deaths from starvation, disease and crime.

The Haitians living in the United States under TPS are hardly a burden on American society. An estimated 200,000 are employed, working as nursing assistants, hotel housekeepers, agricultural workers, cooks, caregivers, and other critical jobs in industries struggling with labor shortages. As a group, Haitians contribute an estimated $5.9 billion to the U.S. economy each year and pay $1.56 billion in federal, payroll, state, and local taxes.

Nor are Haitians, as a group, criminals. According to the non-partisan Cato Institute, Haitian immigrants have an incarceration rate approximately 81 percent below native-born Americans. More broadly, even as the immigrant share of the U.S. population more than doubled from 6.2 percent in 1980 to 13.9 percent in 2022, the total U.S. crime rate dropped by 60 percent over the same period. Simply stated—although there are tragic exceptions—immigrants as a group are significantly more law abiding than the average American.

Yet during his rallies, President Trump has called Haitians a threat to America, claimed they were stealing and eating pets in Springfield, Ohio, alleged they probably have AIDS, and declared they, and others from “shithole countries”, are “poisoning the blood of our country.”

During the 2024 presidential election, J.D. Vance amplified the false claim that Haitian immigrants in Springfield, Ohio were abducting and eating cats and dogs. Springfield’s mayor and police quickly debunked the irresponsible claims. When confronted with the facts, Vance said, "If I have to create stories so that the American media actually pays attention to the suffering of the American people, then that's what I'm going to do."

In its June 26 ruling, the Supreme Court, while ruling in favor of the Trump administration, declared the comments made by Donald Trump, J.D. In 2010, a massive earthquake struck Haiti killing over 220,000 Haitians and leaving more than 1.5 million homeless. Thousands of Haitians were permitted to enter the United States under Temporary Protected Status (TPS), a government program that allows refugees from countries experiencing environmental disaster, armed conflict or other life-threatening conditions to legally live and work temporarily in the United States.

Since the 2010 earthquake, 350,000 Haitian refugees have entered the United States under the TPS designation. The Trump administration, though, rightly points out that TPS is a temporary program. Since taking office, the Trump administration has attempted to deport the Haitians back to their home country, but were blocked by federal courts. The courts ruled that the Department of Homeland Security was unlawfully discriminating against Haitian immigrants on the basis of race.

On June 26, however, the Supreme Court reversed the lower court rulings and ruled that the Trump Administration can cancel the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) designation for Haiti (and Syria) forcing the refugees to return to their native countries.

But according to the United Nations and other reliable sources, the conditions in Haiti today are worse than they were in 2010. Wracked by hurricanes, earthquakes, and crime, Haiti is in a state of collapse. On October 29, 2025, Hurricane Melissa killed forty-three people and damaged or flooded nearly 12,000 houses. Armed gangs control an estimated 80 percent of Port-au-Prince, the national capital. Over 16,000 people have been killed since January 2022 and 1.5 million displaced from their homes. Half of the nation’s 11.9 million people face acute food shortages with 600,000 experiencing famine.

The U.S. State Department, warning Americans not to travel to Haiti, has assigned Haiti a Level 4 Travel Advisory, its highest warning, “due to the risk of crime, terrorism, kidnapping, unrest, and limited health care.” Commercial air travel to the country has been cancelled. For the few U.S. citizens still residing in Haiti, the State Department advises, “Consider hiring a professional security organization.”

Sending 350,000 Haitian refugees back to their native country will almost surely result in many of their deaths from starvation, disease and crime.

The Haitians living in the United States under TPS are hardly a burden on American society. An estimated 200,000 are employed, working as nursing assistants, hotel housekeepers, agricultural workers, cooks, caregivers, and other critical jobs in industries struggling with labor shortages. As a group, Haitians contribute an estimated $5.9 billion to the U.S. economy each year and pay $1.56 billion in federal, payroll, state, and local taxes.

Nor are Haitians, as a group, criminals. According to the non-partisan Cato Institute, Haitian immigrants have an incarceration rate approximately 81 percent below native-born Americans. More broadly, even as the immigrant share of the U.S. population more than doubled from 6.2 percent in 1980 to 13.9 percent in 2022, the total U.S. crime rate dropped by 60 percent over the same period. Simply stated—although there are tragic exceptions—immigrants as a group are significantly more law abiding than the average American.

Yet during his rallies, President Trump has called Haitians a threat to America, claimed they were stealing and eating pets in Springfield, Ohio, alleged they probably have AIDS, and declared they, and others from “shithole countries”, are “poisoning the blood of our country.”

During the 2024 presidential election, J.D. Vance amplified the false claim that Haitian immigrants in Springfield, Ohio were abducting and eating cats and dogs. Springfield’s mayor and police quickly debunked the irresponsible claims. When confronted with the facts, Vance said, "If I have to create stories so that the American media actually pays attention to the suffering of the American people, then that's what I'm going to do."

In its June 26 ruling, the Supreme Court, while ruling in favor of the Trump administration, declared the comments made by Donald Trump, J.D. Vance, and others directed at Haitians were “not overtly racist.” And yet, how could a presidential statement that Haitians were “poisoning the blood of our country”—a phrase that echoes Adolf Hitler's words in Mein Kampf—be dismissed by the Supreme Court as something other than overtly racist?

Introducing Velvet-1: AI Model for Onchain Intelligence

Today, we are commencing training for Velvet-1, our first flagship LLM for onchain intelligence.

Onchain analytics is lagging behind coding and general knowledge reasoning capabilities. For truly effective onchain analytics, LLMs need to be constantly online: monitoring, detecting, and understanding data that is deeply interconnected. This must happen in real time, amidst high-velocity change.

General-purpose models can reason about crypto, markets, and protocols in isolation, but they struggle to understand the full context of onchain & social systems. Their context windows and memory were designed and trained to work with static code and text data, not with onchain and social dynamics.

We have developed new types of layers, context, and training techniques to handle these problems. The model is being developed on large-scale, continuously indexed datasets spanning:
- Full onchain activity across major networks, including transactions, smart contract events, state changes, and mempool signals
- Hyperliquid-specific market data, including perpetual orderbooks, funding rates, liquidations, trader positioning, and flow dynamics
- Social and behavioral signals, including onchain and offchain graphs, wallet clustering, and profile embeddings

Over the coming months, we will share technical updates, evaluation benchmarks, infrastructure notes, and early capability results as Velvet-1 progresses.

Velvet-1 is our first step toward by-design on-chain intelligence.

Precipio, Inc. (@PrecipioDx) (Nasdaq: PRPO) CEO Ilan Danieli details a four-hour rapid AML panel designed to identify actionable mutations in acute leukemia patients.

Acute leukemia can kill within a week of diagnosis, yet the genetic testing that guides treatment often takes 10 to 15 days to return. Precipio, Inc. - Nasdaq: PRPO built a four-hour panel to close that gap.
